title: Read the data
and the store
steps.description: We go through analytics, session recordings and the theme itself, and write down where people drop out. On a migration this is the catalogue, the URLs and what the old platform is doing that Shopify does not.

title: Prioritise by
expected impact
steps.description: Every candidate change gets an estimate of what it is worth and what it costs to build, and the list is ordered by that. You approve the order before anything is built.

title: Build and ship
the change
steps.description: We work in Liquid and theme sections on a development theme, review it with you on real data, and publish. A migration ships the same way, in stages rather than one switch.

title: Measure, then
decide the next
steps.description: We leave the change running long enough to read it, compare it against what we expected, and let the result pick what gets built next. After a migration we watch traffic, rankings and checkout for the first weeks.

items.question: Do you build a store from scratch?
items.answer: No. We work on stores that already run and already have traffic, and on stores moving onto Shopify from another platform. We also do not customise premium themes as a service, do not build Shopify apps, and do not take headless or Shopify Plus work. If you need a store stood up from nothing, we are the wrong studio and will say so on the call.

items.question: Can you edit the checkout?
items.answer: Not on Standard or Advanced plans — checkout.liquid is closed to everyone except Shopify Plus, and we do not work on Plus. What we can change is everything leading into it: the cart drawer and cart page, upsells and cross-sells, shipping and returns messaging, and the trust and payment signals on the product page. In practice that is where most of the drop-off is anyway.

items.question: Do we need to supply designs?
items.answer: Either way works. We can design the pages ourselves against what the data says, or build from a Figma file you supply. If you bring the designs, we will tell you upfront where something is expensive to do at the theme layer, before it gets built.

items.question: What happens to SEO in a migration?
items.answer: Every old URL gets mapped to a new one and a 301 redirect, because Shopify's URL structure is not the one you are coming from. We carry over titles, descriptions and structured data, keep the internal linking intact, and check the sitemap, robots.txt and canonical tags after the cutover. Then we watch crawl errors and rankings for the first weeks and fix what moves.

items.question: How do you decide what to test first?
items.answer: By what the numbers say, not by what anyone in the room prefers. We look at where sessions fall out of the funnel, size what fixing that step is worth, weigh it against the build cost, and start at the top of that list. If the data is not there yet, the first piece of work is getting the measurement right.
